coverage: Scope and map: release range v0.18.1..c1979ed3 (timed/recurring task starts with TTS-1-3 fixes, permission settlement before cooperative cancel, annotation input focus, workflow verification cleanup, v0.19.0 operator knowledge and embedded UI). The capability/authority map in v0.18.0-next.json and v0.18.0-next.md is carried forward; rows below restate it with this range's changes. The concurrent uncommitted design edits (HANDOFF changelog, ideas, specs README, FS-02, FS-03) were excluded and preserved.

Timed and recurring starts (new row): authority is task_arms kind=time (due_at, on_time_only) resolved by ResolveDueTimeArms inside the arm/park transaction, and one task_schedules row advanced by revision compare-and-set in the same transaction that inserts the occurrence task (TS-10.R54-R59). Scenarios: crash between occurrence and advancement (single transaction, so neither or both); long outage (probe: one-year daily two-time lenient schedule enumerates 728 occurrences across the 512 cap in two passes and creates exactly one late task); restart in another zone (next_due_wall rebase on first pass, TTS-1 tests); sleep/stop over a strict start parks as missed start time; overlap with a running occurrence leaves the next ready. Evidence: focused state/server/recurrence tests and the probes listed here passed. Limit: zone change while running applies only after restart (documented TS-10 limit); no native macOS sleep/zone receipt. ARCH-v019-1: a deleted project does not stop its schedules.

Unchanged consumers of the new rows: project archive and agent archive/delete pause schedules lazily at the next due occurrence through scheduleUnavailable; task deletion leaves last_task_id rendered as task removed; occurrence tasks enter the unchanged ready/admission/claim/budget/re-arm/start-attempt machinery as ordinary zero-arm ready rows; quota-reset dispatch and startup start recovery read no schedule state. Project deletion is the uncovered consumer (ARCH-v019-1, probe-confirmed).

DB migration: migrations 61 (columns, partial due index, schedule tables) and 62 (next_due_wall) are additive with non-null defaults; 61 was not rewritten after first commit. Real boundary probe: a database seeded at schema 60 by the v0.18.1 tree (task with a work_result arm) opened by the candidate migrated to 62, kept legacy tasks armed/ready with default schedule fields, and accepted a new time-arm task and schedule.

Saved work: no transcript, projection or reindex code changed in range; prior v0.18.0-next evidence (per-conversation reindex, kill/reopen/retry, ARCH-1 closure) is reused unchanged. No new data-loss claim either way.

Work progress and supervision: due work runs on the existing two-second dispatcher tick before recovery and admission, bounded to taskDispatchBatch, with no timer per row. Armed tasks progress when the last arm resolves in the same transaction (A35 test). Pipeline/room/task-result authority is unchanged; prior evidence reused. Fake/store proof is not native consumption.

Agent tool results report state, rule in words and RFC3339 next occurrence. Physical-phone/native gates remain owed.
